skill.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skill.description: Guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users in splitting independent debugging or implementation work across parallel agents.
skill.summary: Dispatch focused agents for independent coding tasks, then review and integrate their results.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Complex coding sessions slow down when independent failures are investigated one after another. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code split work into focused parallel agent tasks and integrate the results.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when tasks are independent enough for parallel agent work.
Provides a decision flow for choosing parallel, sequential, or single-agent investigation.
Shows how to write focused agent prompts with scope, goals, constraints, and expected output.
Gives examples for splitting failing test files across separate agents.
Defines a review process for summaries, conflicts, full test runs, and spot checks.
Lists common mistakes that make agent tasks too broad or hard to verify.
limitations: Does not create agents automatically without the host tool supporting that workflow.
Does not solve tasks that require shared state or full-system context.
Requires the user to verify agent results and run tests after integration.
Does not provide repository-specific dependency analysis.

use_cases.title: Split Failing Test Files
use_cases.description: Assign independent failing test files to separate agents and compare their root-cause summaries.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Refactor Follow-up
use_cases.description: Handle unrelated breakages after a refactor by giving each agent a constrained subsystem to inspect.

use_cases.title: Teach Agent Workflow Design
use_cases.description: Use the examples to train teams on scoped prompts, constraints, and integration checks.

prompt_templates.title: Find Independent Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failures and group them by independent problem domain. Tell me which groups can be handled by separate agents and why.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Agent Assignments
prompt_templates.scenario: Create focused tasks for multiple agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one agent assignment per independent failure group. Each assignment must include scope, goal, constraints, and expected summary output.

prompt_templates.title: Run Parallel Debugging
prompt_templates.scenario: Use Claude Code or Codex to investigate independent test failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Dispatch parallel agents for these independent test files. Each agent should inspect only its assigned file, identify the root cause, make focused changes, and return a concise summary.

prompt_templates.title: Review Integration Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after several agents return changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these agent summaries and changed files. Identify conflicts, duplicated assumptions, missing tests, and the order needed to integrate the fixes safely.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test files fail after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends one agent per test file, each with a narrow prompt and a required root-cause summary.

output_examples.input: Two failures appear related to the same shared state bug.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a single investigation first, because parallel agents could duplicate work or create conflicting fixes.

output_examples.input: Parallel agents return changes for separate subsystems.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends reading each summary, checking for overlapping edits, running the full suite, and spot-checking assumptions.

best_practices: Dispatch agents only after confirming the tasks are independent.
Give each agent a narrow scope, clear goal, explicit constraints, and expected output.
Review summaries and run the full test suite before accepting combined changes.
anti_patterns: Do not ask one agent to fix all failures when independent domains are available.
Do not dispatch parallel agents when failures share state or likely root causes.
Do not merge agent changes without checking conflicts and verification results.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps split independent coding or debugging work across parallel agents, then review and integrate their results.

faq.question: Does it run agents by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance for tools such as Claude, Codex, and Claude Code that support agent tasks.

faq.question: When should I avoid using it?
faq.answer: Avoid it when failures are related, share state, or require one complete system-level investigation.

faq.question: What should each agent prompt include?
faq.answer: Each prompt should include one scope, one goal, clear constraints, context, and the required return summary.

faq.question: How do I reduce conflicts between agents?
faq.answer: Assign non-overlapping files or subsystems and tell each agent not to change code outside its scope.

faq.question: How should I verify the final result?
faq.answer: Read every summary, inspect changed files for overlap, run the full test suite, and spot-check risky assumptions.
